fields.name: ENABLE
fields.why: xosc_init() does hw_set_bits(&xosc_hw->ctrl, ENABLE_VALUE_ENABLE << ENABLE_LSB) (xosc.c:37). A modeled field must decode the exact 12-bit magic value, not just non-zero -- DISABLE (0xd1e) is also non-zero.

fields.name: FREQ_RANGE
fields.why: 'This resets to 0xAA0 and cannot be changed' per the header comment -- RP2040 silicon only implements the 1-15MHz encoding despite the field being nominally RW; modeled here as plain rw since xosc_init() always writes the same VALUE_1_15MHZ constant (xosc.c:31) and no boot-path firmware exercises the RESERVED encodings.

fields.name: STABLE
fields.why: xosc_init() spins `while(!(xosc_hw->status & XOSC_STATUS_STABLE_BITS)) { tight_loop_contents(); }` (src/rp2_common/hardware_xosc/xosc.c:40-42, fetched this session -- VERIFIED, quoted). Same field polled inverted in xosc_disable() (xosc.c:51-53) and non-inverted again in xosc_dormant() (xosc.c:60-62). This is the FIRST hardware-dependent hang point in a stock boot -- before PLL or CLOCKS are ever touched. Real silicon has a startup delay counted by the STARTUP register's DELAY field (offset 0x0c, not itemized field-by-field here); modeling STABLE as an instant ready-follows rather than a counter-gated delay is a documented simplification, not a correctness gap for boot-to-blink.

fields.name: ENABLED
fields.why: 'Oscillator is enabled but not necessarily running and stable, resets to 0' -- an immediate (not startup-delay-gated) mirror of ENABLE, distinct from STABLE. Not itself polled by any pico-sdk call found this session.
